newsitem.title: USA: Pamida looks for EBIDTA gains in FY98. [CORRECTED 16:10 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Pamida looks for EBIDTA gains in FY98. [CORRECTED 16:10 GMT]

text.p: Pamida Holdings Corp, reporting earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization for the February 2 fourth-quarter of $16.8 million, up from $12.6 million in the same prior quarter, said it looks for further EBITDA gains in fiscal 1998.
Chairman Steven Fishman, in a statement, said he feels comfortable with analysts' fiscal 1998 expectations for improvements in EBITDA.

But Fishman said higher planned expenses in the first quarter of fiscal 1998 as compared with the same period the prior year likely would skew accumulation of the expected higher EBITDA toward the second, third and fourth quarters.
A company spoksman would not elaborate on the amount of improvement expected.

Pamida also said it is completing documentation to enhance its committed line of credit by increasing its borrowing limit to $95 million from $70 million and extending the term of the facility to March 2000.

Earlier Thursday the company, which operates general merchandise stores, reported fiscal 1997 fourth quarter earnings of $0.99 compared to a year-ago loss of $0.26, excluding one-time charges. (Corrects to insert dropped words "fourth quarter")
